source: a free driving train game with only steam engines and where u can spawn train cars such as passenger cars and freight cars anywhere in the world with mounntains hills rivers a weather cycle and a driving GUI where it has speed brakes emergency brakes and a reverser and nice connecting sounds when coupling up to train cars and when u blow the whistle in steam engines it has a nice recording of the New Zealand 5 Chime whistle

answers.ask: No visual theme was stated — should the world read as period New Zealand branch line, generic rural steam era, or stylized toon?
answers.answer: Make it a period New Zealand branch line, matching the New Zealand 5 Chime steam whistle.

answers.ask: How much world do you want — a valley or two, or a continent-sized network you can drive for an hour?
answers.answer: Keep it to a small, playable map with one or two valleys, mountains, hills, and rivers.

answers.ask: Should there be stations, yards, and depots along the line, or is it purely open track?
answers.answer: Include a few simple stations, small yards, and depots along the line so there are useful places to spawn and couple cars.

- [author] theme — Q: No visual theme was stated — should the world read as period New Zealand branch line, generic rural steam era, or stylized toon? A: Make it a period New Zealand branch line, matching the New Zealand 5 Chime steam whistle.
- [author] scale — Q: How much world do you want — a valley or two, or a continent-sized network you can drive for an hour? A: Keep it to a small, playable map with one or two valleys, mountains, hills, and rivers.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a small, playable period New Zealand steam-rail map spanning one or two valleys. Build a connected railway line through mountains and rolling hills, crossing or following several rivers, with a few simple stations, small switching yards, and steam depots along the route. Give yards and depots level sidings long enough to spawn, arrange, and couple steam locomotives, passenger cars, and freight cars. Keep the landscape rural and historical, with no modern diesel or electric rail infrastructure. Compose the rail network, valleys, waterways, stations, yards, and depots clearly from above.

## Genre
Simulation is the dominant genre.

## Shape and preset
Use `world-open`, Shared Persistent World, for one freely driven rural rail map without race laps or a finish. Preset: none; the Vehicle Sim preset's road and resource-field bundle does not describe a railway network.

## Config requirements
No canonical catalogue option describes railway track, so use a free-text Path for one connected main rail line with station sidings, yard branches, and depot spurs. Use `terrain-relief` for the valleys, hills, and mountains, and `water-body` for the rivers. Stations, yards, depots, bridges, track beds, signals, and coupling sidings are direct scene components.

## Layout requirements
Place free-text SpawnZones on level rail sidings at each yard and depot for steam engines, passenger cars, and freight cars, oriented along the rails. Car spawning “anywhere” must snap to valid rail geometry; its UI and dynamic placement are mechanics. Driving controls, brakes, reverser, weather cycle, coupling sounds, and whistle recording are also mechanics rather than placements.

## Layout components
The map contains one or two connected valleys bounded by mountains and hills. One main railway threads through them, with bridges where it crosses rivers and branches only into a few station sidings, small yards, and depot spurs. Every branch rejoins or terminates at a clear buffer. Level coupling ground sits beside stations and depots. The outer mountain landscape forms the boundary, and all track remains visible enough to understand the network.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: continuous rail connections, switches, bridge crossings, yards, and depot spurs must be established before period landscape dressing.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, driven by one or two valleys while preserving stations and train-length sidings. The theme is a period New Zealand rural steam branch line. Use `tiered` for mountain and valley relief and `CHECK` for rivers; no racing `P6`, interior, or separate-map pass applies.

options.text: Valleys, mountains, and rolling hills shaping the rural New Zealand landscape around the railway.
Several rivers the railway follows and/or crosses via bridges through the one or two valleys.

layout.composition: Compose the rail network, valleys, waterways, stations, yards, and depots clearly from above.

zones.name: Valley 1
zones.role: Primary rural valley containing sections of the connected main railway and rivers, with stations/yards/depots along the route.

zones.name: Valley 2
zones.role: Optional second connected valley continuing the railway line and waterways, with additional simple stations/yards/depots.

zones.name: Stations
zones.role: A few simple stations along the main line, with station sidings and level coupling ground beside them.

zones.name: Small yards
zones.role: Small switching yards branching from the main line with level sidings long enough to spawn, arrange, and couple rolling stock; branches rejoin or terminate at a clear buffer.

zones.name: Steam depots
zones.role: Steam depots with depot spurs and level sidings long enough to spawn, arrange, and couple steam locomotives and cars; branches rejoin or terminate at a clear buffer.

zones.name: Outer mountains and hills
zones.role: Mountain and hill landscape bounding the valleys and forming the map boundary; keeps the overall network readable and enclosed by terrain.

layout.terrain: One or two connected valleys bounded by mountains and hills; rolling rural terrain; several rivers crossed or followed by the railway.

props.name: small switching yards
props.where: Branching from the main line, rejoining or terminating at clear buffers.

props.name: steam depots
props.where: Along the route, with depot spurs and level sidings.

props.name: station sidings
props.where: At stations off the main line.

props.name: yard branches
props.where: Branching off the main line into small yards.

props.name: depot spurs
props.where: Branching off the main line into steam depots.

props.name: signals
props.where: Along track as part of the railway scene components.

props.name: buffers
props.where: At the ends of branches that terminate.

layout.boundary: The outer mountain landscape forms the boundary.
layout.theme: Period New Zealand rural steam branch line; historical rural landscape with no modern diesel or electric rail infrastructure.

render.why: Continuous rail connections, switches, bridge crossings, yards, and depot spurs must be established before period landscape dressing.

notes: Blob requests free-text Paths for railway track and free-text SpawnZones on sidings; these are not canonical menu IDs, so they cannot be represented in `options`/`layout_placement` here.
No `where` positions were stated for individual zones beyond general relationships, so several `zones[].where` fields are empty by transcription.

Stage 2 prose implies a second image derived from the first ("dressed after"), but the schema provided here does not include a `render.second` field; only `render.first` and `render.authoritative` are recorded.
Added `P0` to route because the blob calls for `tiered` relief; `tiered` in the menu implies P0.
